newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian jobs figures increase rate cut pressure.
newsitem.headline: Australian jobs figures increase rate cut pressure.

text.p: A larger-than-expected drop in the Australian employment total for September stirred domestic financial markets on Thursday and appeared to increase pressure for an interest rate cut to boost the economy.

Figures from the national Bureau of Statistics showed that the number of people with jobs fell by 34,100 to 8.35 million. Seasonally-adjusted unemployment fell slightly as well, to 8.7 percent from 8.8 percent.

Economists, who had been expecting an employment drop of around 7,500, said the data pointed to a softening of the job market and would increase pressures for an interest rate cut of around half a percentage point.
But most did not expect any cut before a Reserve Bank of Australia board meeting in November after the release of wages and inflation data later this month.
"All we need is a good wages number on the 24th (of October) and then there is a rate cut coming," said Rob Henderson, chief economist at Dresdner Bank.

Employment Minister Amanda Vanstone said the employment figure was a continuation of a year-old trend and predicted that the labour market would remain flat until parliament passed the 1996/97 budget and approved a new industrial relations package.
The Australian dollar fell 0.25 U.S. cents within a few seconds of the announcement and was trading at US$0.7885. After opening lower, bonds jumped on the pressures for a rate cut.
